builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Channel Selection for Mixture-of-Experts Decoding Needs No Calibration Data
summary: Replaces threshold-based, calibration-data-dependent channel selectors for MoE routed experts with a per-token top-k selector and a weight-derived ternary-sketch reader with a low-rank recovery map. Costs include custom Triton kernel integration outside stock vLLM, a roughly 1.9-point average accuracy shortfall relative to the full model, and added implementation complexity in the MoE block. Can fail on models or tasks where top-k channel scoring misranks important channels, and the reported gains are demonstrated on only three post-trained MoE models with specific hardware, so speedups may not transfer.
rationale: The method directly addresses the 24 GB interactive-decoding bottleneck and needs no calibration data, but its gains depend on custom kernels and a small set of validated models, so it warrants a workload-specific pilot before production adoption.
technique: Calibration-free top-k channel selection for MoE decoding

claims.statement: Replaces threshold-based, calibration-data-dependent channel selectors for MoE routed experts with a per-token top-k selector and a weight-derived ternary-sketch reader with a low-rank recovery map. Costs include custom Triton kernel integration outside stock vLLM, a roughly 1.9-point average accuracy shortfall relative to the full model, and added implementation complexity in the MoE block. Can fail on models or tasks where top-k channel scoring misranks important channels, and the reported gains are demonstrated on only three post-trained MoE models with specific hardware, so speedups may not transfer.
Retains 98.1% of full-model accuracy at 17.8% of routed-expert reads; Triton kernels run MoE blocks 1.60 to 1.90x faster than optimized vLLM at batch one and up to 2.69x at larger batches.
